record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special function. Is S right reversible if and only if for every pair A, B in S there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k}∘B^{∘l} and B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l}∘A^{∘k}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.8. Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special function. Then S is right reversible if and only if for any two elements A, B of S there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that the equalities A^{∘2k} = A^{∘k} ∘ B^{∘l}, B^{∘2l} = B^{∘l} ∘ A^{∘k} hold.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting and definitions. Work over the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{CP}^1$. A rational function $A:\mathbb{CP}^1\to\mathbb{CP}^1$ has degree $\deg A$. Composition is denoted $\circ$, and for $k\ge 1$ we write $A^{\circ k}=A\circ A\circ\cdots\circ A$ ($k$ factors). 

A rational function $A$ of degree at least two is called special if either $A$ is conjugate by a Möbius transformation to $z^{\pm n}$ or to a Chebyshev polynomial $\pm T_n$, or $A$ is a Lattès map (a rational function that is semiconjugate to a multiplication-by-$n$ endomorphism of an elliptic curve via a finite-to-one quotient). A rational function is non-special if it is not special.

A semigroup $S$ of rational functions (under composition) is called right reversible if for every $A,B\in S$ there exist $C,D\in S$ such that $A\circ C=B\circ D$ (equivalently, every two principal left ideals $S\circ A$ and $S\circ B$ intersect).

Question. Let $S$ be a semigroup of rational functions, all of degree at least two, that contains at least one non-special function. Is it true that $S$ is right reversible if and only if for every pair $A,B\in S$ there exist integers $k,l\ge 1$ such that
$$A^{\circ 2k}=A^{\circ k}\circ B^{\circ l}\qquad\text{and}\qquad B^{\circ 2l}=B^{\circ l}\circ A^{\circ k}\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture by Pakovich in his 2021 list of problems on semigroups of rational functions. Subsequent work by Pakovich on amenable/reversible semigroups of rational functions (e.g., his "On amenable semigroups of rational functions" and Ann. Fennici Math. 2024 paper) addresses related structural questions, but no source found explicitly confirms a full resolution of this particular equivalence in the non-special case. Status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.snippet: Pakovich studies amenability and reversibility properties for semigroups of rational functions, related to the conjecture under consideration.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related work on reversible/amenable semigroups of rational functions, but no explicit resolution of the conjecture located.

status_evidence.title: Annales Fennici Mathematici 49 (2024), 601–620 (Pakovich)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper continuing the program on semigroups of rational functions and reversibility-type conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Continues the line of investigation but does not visibly settle this exact equivalence.
